findings.comment: Utility plans show electric lines crossing water lines at multiple locations but do not document the required minimum 12-inch (1 foot) horizontal clearance at any crossing point. Provide utility profile sheets or crossing detail drawings for all perpendicular electric-water crossings documenting the separation distance and crossing configuration, or provide documentation confirming all crossings meet or exceed 12 inches horizontal clearance and coordinated with Austin Water requirements.
applicableAreas: Electric-water crossing near southern property boundary
Electric-water crossing in central site area between Buildings 4 and 7
Electric-water crossing in northern site area
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) displays the proposed routing of underground electric lines (shown in yellow per the legend) crossing proposed water lines (shown in cyan) at multiple perpendicular crossing points across the site. Vision analysis identified at least three distinct crossing areas: (1) near the southern property boundary between Buildings 7 and 8, (2) in the central site area between Buildings 4 and 7, and (3) in the northern area. However, the utility tap plan contains no explicit numerical separation dimensions, clearance callouts, or separation specifications at any of these crossing points. The plan notes state only that the contractor must 'field verify locations of utility crossings prior to beginning construction.' No utility profile sheets or crossing detail drawings were identified that document the required 12-inch (1 foot) minimum horizontal clearance at these crossing locations.
findings.reasoning: Electric conduit routing must maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from water lines when crossing perpendicularly per UCM § 1.10.5.A. The utility plans clearly show multiple perpendicular crossings between proposed electric lines and water lines. The absence of any numerical separation dimensions, clearance annotations, or detail drawings showing how these crossings are configured constitutes a failure to document compliance with the minimum clearance requirement. The contractor direction to field-verify does not substitute for design documentation demonstrating compliance on the plans. Without explicit documentation of separation distances or crossing details on the utility plans, the minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified as designed into the project.

findings.comment: Electric conduit and proposed water lines cross at multiple locations on the site (central drive aisle, north/south perimeters). Provide utility profile sheets or crossing detail sections for all electric/water line intersections showing minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical separation, or specify concrete encasement and protection measures at crossing points per UCM § 1.10.5.A.

While the site plan clearly shows electric and water lines crossing at multiple locations, the provided plans do not include profile details, vertical clearance dimensions, or crossing detail sections that would allow verification of compliance with the 12-inch minimum clearance requirement. Without profile sheets or crossing detail specifications, it cannot be determined from the available evidence whether the required clearances are maintained or whether any utility coordination/encasement is specified.

findings.comment: Proposed underground electric line is shown crossing proposed water lines on the utility tap plan (Sheet 20, plan view), but no horizontal clearance dimension is documented at the crossing point. applicableAreas: Water line utility tap public plan and profile crossing location
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows both a plan view (top portion) and a profile view (bottom portion) for the proposed water line labeled 'Wtr-Ln-A' connecting to an existing 8-inch water main. The plan view (Block 2) clearly depicts a proposed underground electric line marked with the symbol '- E -' in the legend defined as 'Proposed Underground Electric.' This electric line is drawn crossing over the water utility lines in the plan view, positioned to the east of the meter vault. The profile shows water line flowline elevations but omits the electrical facility from the profile section entirely, leaving the vertical relationship completely undocumented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires electric conduit routing to maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from water lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan documentation shows an electric line crossing water utility lines in plan view, confirming that a crossing condition exists. However, the plans provide no dimension callout or note documenting the horizontal clearance at this crossing point. The requirement is to show separation of at least 12 inches horizontally, and this required information is absent from the submitted plans. Required information is missing—specifically, the horizontal separation distance at the crossing is not documented. This is a deficiency per the standard that 'required information is absent from the plans (missing elements are deficiencies).'

findings.comment: Utility plans show electric lines running parallel to and crossing wastewater lines throughout the site but do not document the required minimum 12-inch (1 foot) horizontal clearance at any location. Provide utility profile sheets and/or coordination drawings for the extended parallel run behind Buildings 1, 2, 3 and for all perpendicular electric-wastewater crossings documenting the separation distance, or provide documentation confirming all configurations meet or exceed 12 inches horizontal clearance and are coordinated with Austin Water requirements.

Electric-wastewater crossing near central site area

Vision analysis identified two critical areas: (1) Behind Buildings 1, 2, and 3, the electric line runs parallel to the wastewater line for approximately 150-200 feet with the lines appearing to be within only a few feet of each other laterally based on visual scaling at 1 inch = 20 feet, and (2) a perpendicular crossing occurs in the central site area. However, no explicit numerical separation dimensions are called out on the utility plan at either the parallel run or crossing locations. The utility notes state only that the contractor must 'field verify locations of utility crossings prior to beginning construction.' No utility profile sheets or coordination drawings document the horizontal (or vertical) separation at these locations.
findings.reasoning: Electric conduit routing must maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from wastewater lines when crossing perpendicularly per UCM § 1.10.5.A. The utility plans clearly show electric and wastewater utilities in close proximity both as parallel runs and at crossing points. The absence of numerical separation dimensions, clearance callouts, or detail drawings at any of these locations constitutes failure to document design compliance. The extensive parallel run behind Buildings 1, 2, and 3 requires particular documentation of maintained clearance. The contractor directive to field-verify does not substitute for design documentation showing the separation is adequate before construction.

findings.comment: Electric conduit and proposed wastewater lines cross at multiple locations (central drive aisle, courtyard, perimeters). findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal and vertical clearance between electric conduit and wastewater lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan shows electric and wastewater lines crossing at multiple locations, but the provided documentation does not include profile sheets, crossing detail sections, or clearance specifications that would verify compliance with the 12-inch minimum requirement. Without crossing profiles or details, the vertical and horizontal separations at crossing points cannot be verified from the available evidence.

findings.comment: Proposed underground electric conduit is routed through the same utility corridors as proposed wastewater service lines, indicating crossings will occur, but no horizontal clearance dimensions are documented at the crossing locations. Provide plan dimensions or detail notes demonstrating that electric conduit maintains at least 12 inches horizontal clearance from wastewater service lines at all crossing points.
applicableAreas: Proposed wastewater service lines and internal utility routing

findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires electric conduit routing to maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from wastewater lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan documents show proposed wastewater lines and proposed electric routing through the same general utility corridors and crossing areas, confirming that crossings will occur. However, no sheet provides documented horizontal clearance dimensions at these crossing points. Required information (horizontal separation distances of at least 12 inches at each crossing) is absent from the plans. This constitutes a deficiency per the standard that 'required information is absent from the plans.'

findings.comment: Plans show water and wastewater lines crossing underground electric facilities at multiple locations but do not provide utility profile sheets documenting the required minimum 12-inch (1 foot) vertical clearance at any crossing. Provide utility profile sections for all electric-water and electric-wastewater crossing locations showing vertical relationships, flowline/centerline elevations, and separations, or provide coordination documentation confirming all crossings meet or exceed 12 inches vertical clearance.
applicableAreas: All electric-water crossing locations
All electric-wastewater crossing locations
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows the water line profile from the street tap to the property meter vault, with flowline elevations provided. However, this sheet only addresses the public water connection, not the internal site water routing. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows multiple locations where water and wastewater lines cross electric lines throughout the site. However, no internal utility profile sheets were located that document the vertical relationships and clearances at any of these crossing points. The utility plans (Sheets 12, 19) lack any profile views showing vertical separations at crossings. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) includes a reference 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but no detailed profiles with vertical clearance dimensions are evident in either sheet.
findings.reasoning: Proposed water and wastewater lines must maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) vertical clearance from underground electric facilities at crossing points per UCM § 1.10.5.A. The horizontal plans clearly show multiple water-electric and wastewater-electric crossings throughout the site. However, no utility profile sheets documenting the vertical relationships and clearances at these crossing locations were identified. The absence of profile sheets showing which utility passes above/below and documenting the vertical separation distance constitutes failure to document design compliance with the vertical clearance requirement. Profiles are essential to verify vertical clearances when utilities cross.

findings.comment: Utility profile sheets or crossing detail sections must be provided for all locations where proposed water and wastewater lines cross underground electric facilities, showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance and confirming which utility is positioned above the other. Provide elevation data and crossing detail sections per UCM § 1.10.5.A.
applicableAreas: Central drive aisle, north perimeter, courtyard
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) show that underground electric facilities and both water and wastewater lines are present and will cross at multiple locations on site. However, no utility profile sheets or vertical clearance detail sections are provided. Sheet 20 shows water line profile (Water Line A) with flowline elevations but does not show electric line elevations or vertical separation at crossing points. Without cross-sectional details or profile views showing the vertical relationship between electric and water/wastewater utilities at crossing points, vertical clearances cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 1 foot (12 inches) vertical clearance from underground electric facilities to water and wastewater lines at crossing points. While the plans confirm that these utilities cross, the provided documentation does not include utility profile sheets showing the vertical elevation relationships at crossing locations. This is essential information to verify compliance. The absence of crossing profiles makes it impossible to confirm that minimum vertical clearances are maintained from the available evidence.

findings.comment: Proposed water line crosses proposed underground electric line on the utility tap public plan (Sheet 20), but the vertical clearance between the facilities at the crossing point is not documented in the profile view. Add the proposed electric line to the profile view and provide a vertical clearance dimension demonstrating that the water line maintains at least 1 foot minimum vertical clearance from the underground electric facility at the crossing location.
applicableAreas: Water utility tap connection area and internal distribution
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) provides both a plan view and a profile view for the proposed water line utility connection. The plan view (Block 2) clearly shows a label '- E -' (representing Proposed Underground Electric per the legend) crossing through the utility tap area east of the meter vault, intersecting with the proposed water line routing. A notation labeled 'Proximity Call' appears on the plan view but provides no specific measurement or clearance dimension. The profile view (Block 1) shows the water line ('Wtr-Ln-A') with flowline elevations documented at key locations (FL 8" = 674.33' at the entry point, and FL 8" = 671.42' and FL Out 6" = 671.42' near the meter vault). However, the profile view does NOT show the proposed underground electric line crossing, meaning the vertical clearance between the water line and the electric line at the crossing point is completely undocumented. The 'Proximity Call' label appears to be a placeholder for coordination but contains no dimensional information.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires that water lines crossing underground electric facilities maintain minimum 1 foot (12 inches) vertical clearance. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant through plan documentation. Sheet 20 plan view indicates that an electric crossing will occur (shown by the '- E -' line), and the 'Proximity Call' notation suggests the designer was aware of a proximity concern. However, the profile view—which is the correct tool for showing vertical clearance at utility crossings—completely omits the electric line from the section. No vertical clearance dimension, arc, or note documents the separation at this crossing. The applicant has failed to demonstrate compliance with the vertical clearance requirement. This is a clear deficiency: required information (vertical clearance dimensions at the water-electric crossing) is absent from the plans, and missing elements are deficiencies per the evaluation standards.

findings.comment: Storm sewer plan shows multiple drain inlets throughout the site, and utility plan shows electric lines in the same areas with convergence in central site (Bldgs 4-7). No documentation verifies that drain inlets maintain required clearances from underground electric facilities or resolves any conflicts. Provide utility coordination documentation showing all drain inlet locations relative to electric lines and confirming required clearances, or revise inlet locations to avoid conflicts with electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Drainage inlets throughout site in proximity to electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows multiple grate inlets distributed throughout the site (documented as 18-inch and 2'x2' grate inlets at various locations with rim and flowline elevations). Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows the proposed electric line routing throughout the site with blue solid lines. Vision analysis identified a complex area where utilities converge between Buildings 4 and 7, including the storm drain system. However, the utility plans do not provide explicit documentation showing the separation distance between any drain inlet and the underground electric lines at that location. The plans only include a contractor directive to 'field verify locations of utility crossings prior to beginning construction.'
findings.reasoning: Proposed drain inlets must not conflict with existing underground electric facilities without verification of required clearances per UCM § 1.10.5.B. While the plans show both drain inlets and electric lines, there is no documented verification of clearances or conflict resolution at any inlet location. Because drain inlets are excavated structures requiring surface access, their placement relative to underground electric facilities must be verified and documented on the plans, particularly in areas where electric lines and storm drain converge.

findings.comment: Multiple storm drain inlets are proposed within 5 feet of underground electric facilities. Specifically, courtyard inlets conflict with transformer pads, and the inlet west of Building 2 is positioned directly adjacent to the electrical utility line. Revise drain inlet locations to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all underground electric facilities, or coordinate with Austin Energy for encasement/protection measures if clearance cannot be achieved.
applicableAreas: Courtyard area between Buildings 4-7, near Building 2, near Buildings 7-8
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and cross-reference with Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) reveals multiple storm drain inlets positioned directly adjacent to or within close proximity of underground electrical infrastructure. Specific conflicts identified: (1) Central courtyard area contains four 18" grate inlets (Rim elevations 683.13, 683.15, 682.95, 683.10) positioned in the central landscaped/hardscape courtyard where transformer pads are located; (2) West of Building 2, an 18" grate inlet (Rim 683.82) is positioned directly adjacent to the "E" (electrical) utility line running along the western boundary; (3) South of Buildings 7 and 8, a series of 2'x2' grate inlets (Rims 679.30, 679.94, 680.99) are located in the drive aisle directly in proximity to electrical infrastructure serving those buildings. These drain inlets are located within the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone required between underground electric facilities and other site improvements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to site improvements and hardscape features. Storm drain inlets are site drainage improvements that require clearance from electrical infrastructure. The courtyard inlets appear to be directly adjacent to or within the transformer pad areas, and the Building 2 inlet is positioned directly on the electrical line corridor. Visual analysis at the 1" = 20' scale indicates these inlets fall within 5 feet (and likely within 0-3 feet) of the electrical conduit and transformer pads. This represents a coordination failure between drainage design and electrical routing.

findings.comment: Utility plans show Austin Water infrastructure (water and wastewater lines) in close proximity to electric utilities throughout the site (particularly a 150-200 foot parallel run behind Buildings 1-3 and convergence in central site area) but do not document the required minimum 5-foot horizontal separation for trench integrity. Provide utility coordination sheets documenting the separation between all Austin Water infrastructure and non-Austin Water utilities (electric, storm drain), or revise utility routing to achieve and document 5-foot separation per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2.
applicableAreas: Electric-water separation in central site corridor
Electric-wastewater separation throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows water lines (cyan) provided by Austin Water and wastewater lines (magenta) both crossing and running in proximity to proposed electric lines (yellow). Vision analysis noted that 'Behind Bldgs 1, 2, and 3: yellow Electric line runs parallel and extremely close to magenta Wastewater line for roughly 150-200 feet. Given the scale, they appear to be within a very few feet of each other laterally.' Additionally, the vision analysis identified a central crossing area where multiple utilities including water and electric converge with no documented separations. However, the utility plan contains no explicit separation dimensions between Austin Water infrastructure and non-Austin Water (electric) infrastructure at any location. The plan only includes a general contractor note to field-verify utility locations.
findings.reasoning: Minimum horizontal separation of 5 feet must be maintained between Austin Water infrastructure and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2. The utility plan shows Austin Water lines (water and wastewater) running in proximity to electric lines throughout the site, with the parallel run behind Buildings 1, 2, 3 appearing to be within only a few feet based on visual scale. No separation dimensions are documented on the utility plan. This failure to document the required separation violates the trench integrity requirement of the code.

findings.comment: Water and wastewater utilities from Austin Water are routed through the site in proximity to non-Austin Water infrastructure (electric and storm drain), but no separation distances are documented on the utility plans showing compliance with the minimum 5-foot horizontal separation requirement or the 3-foot residential service line exception. Provide dimension callouts or notes on the utility plans documenting that Austin Water infrastructure is separated from non-AW infrastructure by at least 5 feet (or 3 feet if residential service lines), as required.
applicableAreas: Utility corridors where Austin Water (water/wastewater) and non-AW infrastructure (electric, storm drain) run in proximity
findings.observation: The site plan documents show multiple utility types routed through similar areas of the property: Sheet 19 shows water (W) and wastewater (WW) lines (Austin Water infrastructure) routed through the central drive aisles; Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines (non-AW infrastructure) forming a perimeter loop; Sheet 20 indicates an electric crossing over water facilities. The plans do not provide any dimension callouts, notes, or specifications documenting the horizontal separation distances between Austin Water infrastructure and non-AW infrastructure (particularly electric) in the utility corridors. UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires 5 feet minimum horizontal separation between Austin Water mains and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure, with an exception allowing 3 feet for residential service lines only. No plan view or detail shows measured separations meeting either the 5-foot requirement or the 3-foot residential exception with supporting documentation of which requirement applies and at what locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum horizontal separation of 5 feet between Austin Water infrastructure and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure to maintain trench integrity, with an exception allowing 3 feet for residential service lines only. The site plan shows both Austin Water utilities (water and wastewater) and non-AW utilities (electric and storm drain) sharing utility corridors. However, no plan view provides documented separation distances between these utilities. The plans lack dimension callouts, notes, or specifications indicating that either the 5-foot standard separation or the 3-foot residential service line exception has been verified and applied. Without plan-based documentation of these required separations, compliance cannot be confirmed. This is an unclear determination because the available evidence is insufficient to verify that the requirement is met.

findings.comment: Plan and profile exhibits showing proximity to existing electrical facilities and how transformer routing/underground electric lines cross other utilities are not provided. Create profile views on the Utility Tap Plan or a separate electrical profile sheet showing: (1) how underground electric lines cross stormwater, wastewater, and water utilities; (2) elevations and depths of electrical routing; (3) clearances from existing utilities.
applicableAreas: Wet Utilities Plan
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has a legend that includes electrical symbols but contains zero actual electrical infrastructure depicted on the plan. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows only a water tap connection profile to the public right-of-way, with no electrical profile. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 contains no electrical routing or transformer details. Vision analysis confirmed: 'No profile (cross-sectional) views on this sheet' and 'zero electrical infrastructure is drawn on this specific sheet' for Sheet 19.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires plan and profile exhibits showing proximity to existing electrical facilities. This is essential to identify potential conflicts between new transformer/electrical routing and existing utilities. Sheet 21 contains a reference directing to Sheet 19 for profile information, but Sheet 19 does not provide electrical profiles. No plan and profile exhibits are provided showing how the proposed electrical infrastructure relates to existing facilities or how it crosses other utilities.

findings.comment: Profile showing how transformer routing and underground electric lines cross stormwater piping is not provided. Sheet 21 references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 contains no electrical infrastructure. Provide cross-sectional profile(s) showing: (1) the vertical alignment of underground electric lines at points where they cross storm drain pipes; (2) depths of each utility; (3) clearances between utilities; (4) any separations or protection required for safe co-location.
applicableAreas: Utility Profiles - Sheet 19 or 20
findings.observation: Sheet 21 explicitly references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' in a callout directing readers to Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) for profile information on transformer routing. However, vision analysis of Sheet 19 confirmed: 'No profile (cross-sectional) views on this sheet. The entire drawing is a single plan (top-down) view.' Additionally, 'zero electrical infrastructure is drawn on this specific sheet' - the legend includes electrical symbols but they are not used in the actual plan. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) contains only water line profiles, not electrical. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows storm drainage system but no electrical routing crossing information.
findings.reasoning: When electrical routing crosses stormwater piping, a profile or cross-section must show the vertical relationship, depths, and clearances. Sheet 21 directs readers to Sheet 19 for this profile, but Sheet 19 contains no electrical information whatsoever. This is a critical coordination gap - without profiles showing how electrical routing crosses storm drain lines, depth conflicts cannot be identified and safe installation cannot be ensured.

findings.comment: Utility and storm drain plans show electric lines crossing storm drain lines at multiple locations (including a dense cluster between Buildings 4-7) but do not document the required minimum 12-inch (1 foot) clearance at any crossing. Provide utility profile sheets and crossing details for all electric-storm drain crossings documenting separation distance, or provide documentation confirming all crossings meet or exceed 12 inches horizontal clearance.
applicableAreas: Electric-storm drain crossing in central site area
Electric-utility crossings throughout site
findings.observation: Sheets 12 (Storm Sewer Plan), 19 (Utility Tap Plan), and 21 (Electrical Design Plan) collectively show proposed electric lines (yellow on Sheet 19) crossing storm drain lines (green on Sheet 19, shown as dashed lines on Sheet 12) at multiple locations. Vision analysis of Sheet 19 identified a tight cluster where electric, water, and storm drain lines all converge in the central crossing area between Buildings 4 and 7. Additionally, electric lines cross storm drain lines at other locations throughout the site. However, none of the utility plans contain explicit numerical separation dimensions, clearance specifications, or crossing detail drawings at any of these crossing points. The storm drain plan note (Block 13, Sheet 12) states only that 'Contractor shall field verify locations of utility crossings prior to beginning construction.'
findings.reasoning: Electric conduit routing must maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from other private utilities (excluding gas, fuel, steam) when crossing perpendicularly per UCM § 1.10.5.A. The plans clearly show electric-storm drain crossings at multiple locations, including in a congested area where multiple utilities converge (Bldgs 4-7 area). The complete absence of numerical separation dimensions, clearance callouts, or crossing detail drawings at any crossing location represents a failure to document design compliance. Storm drain is specifically a utility that requires documented separation. The contractor directive to field-verify does not substitute for design documentation demonstrating adequate clearance before construction.

findings.comment: Utility plans show water, wastewater, electric, and storm drain utilities all routed through the same internal drive corridor rather than being separated by type to opposite sides of the roadway. Provide utility coordination documentation addressing the mixture of wet and dry utilities in the same corridor, or revise routing to separate wet utilities (water, wastewater) to one side of the roadway and dry utilities (electric, storm drain, communications) to the opposite side per standard utility separation practice.
applicableAreas: Internal roadway corridor containing multiple utility types
findings.observation: Sheets 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and 19 (Utility Tap Plan) show that water (W), wastewater (WW), electric (E), and storm drain (SD) utilities all run through the same internal roadway corridor(s) on the site. Specifically, vision analysis noted that utilities 'all converge in the central crossing area between Buildings 4 and 7.' The utility plans show wet utilities (water from Austin Water, wastewater) and dry utilities (electric) routed along the same internal drive loop rather than being separated to opposite sides of the roadway. No notes on the utility plans document that wet and dry utilities are properly grouped and alternated on opposite sides of the roadway for safety purposes, nor is there any documented coordination showing this mixing has been evaluated and is acceptable.
findings.reasoning: Wet and dry utilities should be properly grouped and alternated (wet utilities on one side of roadway, dry utilities on opposite side) for safety purposes per Reviewer Convention. The utility routing shown clearly places both wet and dry utilities in the same corridor running through the internal site loop. The absence of any note or coordination documentation indicating this arrangement has been evaluated or is acceptable for this site represents a failure to document compliance with the utility separation convention.

findings.comment: Three storm drain manholes are located directly in pedestrian sidewalk areas and vehicle driveway paths. Relocate manholes to utility easement areas outside of primary circulation routes, or modify site plan to accommodate manhole access without creating conflicts with pedestrian routes, ramps, or vehicle drives.
applicableAreas: Central area between Buildings 7-8, between Buildings 2-3, south of Building 7
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) identifies three storm drain manholes with locations that conflict with pedestrian and vehicular site features: (1) SD Manhole between Buildings 2 and 3 (Rim 684.71): Located in a landscaped/pedestrian area directly adjacent to a north-south sidewalk routing, creating a maintenance access conflict and potential trip hazard in a pedestrian circulation path; (2) SD Manhole between Buildings 7 and 8 (Rim 683.78): Located in a paved pedestrian sidewalk threshold connecting the southern parking area to the central courtyard, directly in a pedestrian travel path; (3) SD Manhole south of Building 7 (Rim 681.02): Located directly in the paved vehicle driveway path, a primary vehicle circulation area. These manhole locations overlap with primary site circulation routes rather than being positioned in dedicated utility access areas.
findings.reasoning: Manhole placement must not conflict with site features that require vertical transitions (stairs, ramps, accessible routes) and should not be located directly in high-traffic pedestrian or vehicular circulation paths. The three manholes are positioned in: one in a pedestrian sidewalk area, one directly in a pedestrian pathway serving multiple buildings, and one in a primary vehicle driveway. These locations create conflicts with site circulation, accessibility, maintenance access, and pose potential trip hazards. Manhole covers in circulation paths are a code compliance issue and accessibility/safety concern.

findings.comment: Proposed underground electric line is shown crossing proposed water utility line on Sheet 20, but no concrete encasement detail or Austin Energy Design approval documentation is provided. Either provide a detail showing 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the electric/water crossing, or provide written confirmation from Austin Energy Design that encasement is not required for this crossing.
applicableAreas: Proposed electric utility crossing water facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows a proposed underground electric line (marked '- E -' in the legend, defined as 'Proposed Underground Electric') crossing the proposed water line in the plan view east of the meter vault area. The crossing is indicated by the intersection of the electric line graphic with the water line graphic on the plan portion of the sheet. However, no detail sheet, profile view, or note on Sheet 20 or any related sheet reviewed documents or specifies concrete encasement requirements at this crossing point. Specifically, there is no detail showing 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the crossing, nor is there any note referencing Austin Energy Design approval of the crossing configuration. The utility notes on Sheet 20 (Block 8) contain only general contractor verification directives and do not address the specific encasement requirement for electric conduit crossings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A specifies that when electric conduit crosses other utilities, it shall have 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the crossing point, or encasement shall be verified as not required through Austin Energy Design approval. The site plan documents show an electric crossing occurring (Sheet 20 plan view), but no detail, note, or reference documentation is provided showing either: (1) the concrete encasement specification, or (2) written confirmation from Austin Energy Design that encasement is not required. Required information is missing from the plans. This is a deficiency because the applicant has not documented either the encasement detail or the design approval that would exempt this crossing from the encasement requirement.

findings.comment: Proposed conduit routing is not shown in profile/section view. Sheet 21 references Sheet 19 for profiles, but Sheet 19 contains no electrical profiles. Please provide detailed utility profile sections showing proposed electric conduit routing with: (1) depth of burial, (2) clearance from other utilities, (3) clearance from existing structures, and (4) elevation coordination with site grading.
applicableAreas: All utility profile sheets
findings.observation: Sheet 21 contains notation 'See Sheet 19 for Profile' directing readers to utility profile information. However, vision analysis of Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) revealed NO profile/section views of any utilities—only plan view drawing with tables. Sheet 19 shows water, wastewater, and storm drain linework and callouts but no vertical cross-sections or profiles. Examination of other sheets (Storm Sewer Plan, Biofiltration Pond Profiles) found drainage and pond profiles but no electric utility profiles.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires proposed conduit routing to be shown in profile view. The reference on Sheet 21 to Sheet 19 for profile information appears to be a cross-sheet coordination error—Sheet 19 lacks any electrical profiles. Conduit depth of burial, clearance from other utilities, and elevation coordination cannot be verified without profile views showing the underground electric routing in cross-section.

findings.comment: Cross-section details not provided where storm drains and water lines cross underground electric conduit and facilities. Provide cross-section details at all utility crossing locations showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance (24-36 inches for gas/fuel/steam lines) and horizontal separation per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: Proposed storm drain and water line crossings with underground electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows a profile view of the proposed water line and a plan view indicating the location of proposed underground electric facilities (marked as 'Proposed Underground Electric' with transformer pad symbol). The vision analysis of Sheet 20 confirmed that the plan view shows both water utility and electric utility at the same general location, indicating a crossing or potential conflict. However, the profile view on Sheet 20 only depicts the water line elevations; there is NO cross-section detail showing the vertical relationship, clearance distance, or separation between the water line and the electric conduit at the crossing point. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) would show storm drain routing, and if it crosses the proposed underground electric lines shown on Sheet 21, a cross-section detail should be provided. No such detail has been located.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires cross-section details where utilities cross AE underground facilities to demonstrate required clearances. The grouping specifies that when storm drains and water lines cross underground electric lines, cross-section details must be provided showing vertical and horizontal clearance verification. The preliminary electrical plan and utility tap plan show the general locations and routing of utilities, but without cross-section details at crossing locations, the vertical and horizontal clearances cannot be verified. This is a documentation deficiency - the required cross-section views must be provided to demonstrate compliance with utility separation requirements.

findings.comment: Cross-section utility design drawings not provided showing vertical and horizontal clearances between underground electric lines and crossing utilities (water, wastewater, storm drainage). Provide cross-section details for each utility crossing showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance for water/wastewater and minimum clearance distances per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: Utility crossings between underground electric lines and water, wastewater, and storm drainage facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows the water utility tap plan and profile but does NOT provide cross-section details showing vertical and horizontal clearances at locations where the water line intersects with the proposed underground electric facilities shown on Sheet 21. Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing throughout the site, and Sheet 20 shows proposed water line routing. These utilities are indicated as crossing or in close proximity in the plan view, but no cross-section engineering drawings are provided demonstrating the specific clearance dimensions at crossing locations. The vision analysis of Sheet 20 confirmed that while utilities are shown in plan view, no cross-section details are provided showing utility separation and clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires that where utilities cross AE underground facilities, cross-section details must be provided that show both vertical and horizontal clearances. These clearances must be dimensioned and verified: minimum 12 inches for water/wastewater, 24-36 inches for gas/fuel/steam, and 12 inches for other utilities. The absence of cross-section views at utility crossing locations is a clear documentation deficiency. The applicant must provide cross-section drawings (not just plan views) showing the three-dimensional relationship of utilities at crossing points to verify clearance compliance. Without these details, the design cannot be verified as compliant.

findings.comment: Elevations not provided on utility crossing details where electric facilities cross storm drains and water lines. Provide cross-section details with vertical elevation dimensions showing how utilities cross and the separation distance maintained between them.
applicableAreas: Utility crossing locations throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) includes a profile view of the water line showing vertical elevations (labeled with flowline elevations such as 'FL 8": 674.33'), demonstrating that elevation information is available for water utilities. However, the profile view only depicts the water line and does not show the underground electric facility at crossing locations. No cross-section details with elevation dimensions are provided at locations where utilities cross. The vision analysis confirmed that while the water line profile includes elevation callouts, there are no elevation-detailed cross-sections showing the utility crossing locations or the relative elevations of the electric and water utilities at those points.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires that elevations be provided on utility crossings to demonstrate clearance compliance. The grouping specifies 'Elevations not provided on utility crossings' as a deficiency. While Sheet 20 provides a profile with elevations for the water line, it does not provide cross-sectional details with elevations at the actual crossing point with the electric utility. The absence of elevation dimensions at utility crossing locations prevents verification of the vertical clearance requirement. Cross-section details with labeled elevations for both utilities at crossing points must be provided.

findings.comment: Provide plan and profile exhibits showing transformer locations, elevations, and proximity to existing electrical facilities and other buried utilities to verify clearances and identify conflicts.
applicableAreas: electrical design plan
wet utilities plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric routing (blue lines) connecting service stubs to transformers and meters in plan view only. Sheet 21 references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains only water and wastewater utility profiles; no electrical profiles are provided. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) similarly shows only water utility profiles in the 'Wtr-Ln-A' section. No profile view showing transformer locations, elevations, or proximity to existing electrical facilities (such as overhead transmission lines, underground utilities at depth, or utility conflicts) is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires 'georeferenced AutoCAD drawings that clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations, demonstrate sufficient clearances, and show access routes.' Plan and profile exhibits showing vertical relationships (elevations, depths, clearances) are necessary to demonstrate compliance with separation distances and to identify conflicts with other utilities. Vertical profiles showing how electrical routing crosses or interfaces with storm drain, water, wastewater, and other buried infrastructure are essential for construction sequencing and conflict resolution.

findings.comment: Provide profile view(s) showing how underground electrical routing crosses storm drain piping, including crossing location, elevation differences, separation distance, and any special protection required at crossing points.
applicableAreas: electrical design plan
storm sewer plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) contains a note: 'See Sht. 19 for Profile.' However, Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) is a water/wastewater utility sheet and contains no electrical profiles. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows storm drain piping routing and details but does not overlay or cross-reference electrical routing. No profile view is provided that shows electrical conduit or cables crossing or running parallel to storm drain piping, including identification of crossing points, separation distances, or special construction details required at crossings.
findings.reasoning: When underground electrical routing crosses stormwater piping, special design considerations are required including clearance distances, use of conduit sleeves or casings at crossing points, and coordination of excavation depths. Per UCM § 1.16.0, 'georeferenced drawings' must clearly show these interactions. Without profiles showing electrical-storm drain crossings, the design cannot be reviewed for compliance with electrical and drainage standards, and the contractor cannot identify required construction sequences or protection measures.
